note: PDF API defines a PdfGenerator plugin type (manager plugin.manager.pdf_generator, dir Plugin/PdfGenerator, annotation @PdfGenerator, interface PdfGeneratorInterface, base PdfGeneratorBase) with bundled backends dompdf/mpdf/tcpdf/wkhtmltopdf. Its only bundled UI is the Dompdf settings form (route pdf_api.settings at /admin/config/system/pdf-api, permission 'administer site configuration') persisting to the config object pdf_api.dom_pdf.settings. Medium/hard cases are grounded in that real config object (keys dpi, defaultFont, isRemoteEnabled, isJavascriptEnabled with shipped defaults 96 / serif / true / true); introspection reads a known value back, execution changes a value and verifies the live config. No shared entities are touched, so cases are namespaced by using only pdf_api's own config.

evals.prompt: On a Drupal 11 site with the pdf_api (PDF API) module, where are the Dompdf backend settings stored and at what admin path are they edited?
evals.expected_output: The Dompdf settings form (route pdf_api.settings) lives at /admin/config/system/pdf-api and saves to the config object pdf_api.dom_pdf.settings (keys such as defaultFont, dpi, pdfBackend, isRemoteEnabled, isJavascriptEnabled).

evals.prompt: Which PDF generator backends ship with the Drupal pdf_api module, and how would I load one from code to generate a PDF?
evals.expected_output: Four backends ship: dompdf, mpdf, tcpdf, wkhtmltopdf (plus puphpeteer from the submodule). Load one via the plugin manager service plugin.manager.pdf_generator, e.g. \Drupal::service('plugin.manager.pdf_generator')->createInstance('dompdf'), then call addPage()/save()/stream().

evals.prompt: How do I add a brand-new PDF backend to the Drupal pdf_api module? Name the plugin annotation, the directory plugins are discovered from, and the interface/base class to use.
evals.expected_output: Create a plugin class in src/Plugin/PdfGenerator/ annotated with @PdfGenerator (id, module, title, description, required_class), implementing Drupal\pdf_api\Plugin\PdfGeneratorInterface and extending PdfGeneratorBase. The manager plugin.manager.pdf_generator discovers it; clear caches to register.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site's pdf_api Dompdf backend has had its image DPI changed from the default. Inspect the live pdf_api configuration and state the current DPI value and the current default font.
evals.expected_output: In pdf_api.dom_pdf.settings the dpi is 150 (default is 96) and defaultFont is 'DejaVu Sans'. Read with: drush cget pdf_api.dom_pdf.settings dpi.

evals.prompt: For security review: on this site, is the Dompdf backend of pdf_api currently allowed to load remote images/stylesheets? Inspect the live configuration and answer which setting controls it and its current value.
evals.expected_output: No — isRemoteEnabled is false in pdf_api.dom_pdf.settings (default is true). Read with: drush cget pdf_api.dom_pdf.settings isRemoteEnabled.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, configure the pdf_api Dompdf backend so that generated PDFs use an image DPI of 300 and a default font of 'sans-serif'. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: In pdf_api.dom_pdf.settings set dpi to 300 (integer) and defaultFont to 'sans-serif' (e.g. drush cset -y pdf_api.dom_pdf.settings dpi 300 and drush cset -y pdf_api.dom_pdf.settings defaultFont sans-serif, or via the form at /admin/config/system/pdf-api).

evals.prompt: Harden the pdf_api Dompdf backend on this site by disabling inline JavaScript execution in generated PDFs. Apply the change to the live configuration.
evals.expected_output: In pdf_api.dom_pdf.settings set isJavascriptEnabled to false (drush cset -y pdf_api.dom_pdf.settings isJavascriptEnabled 0, or untick 'Enable inline JavaScript' on the form). The default is true.
